encodingDesc.p: Printed small capitals transcribed in uppercase; ordinary line-wrap hyphenation joined explicitly; lexical hyphens, spelling, punctuation, brackets and printed footnote pointers retained. Raw digital HTML/XML, scan crops and source bytes remain recoverable. Comparisons may fold case and ae/æ; original source readings are retained without such folding.

normalization.p: Sentence-case presentation is an editorial layer, not a replacement transcription. Each choice retains the exact accepted 1856 text in orig and a case-only display in reg. Proper names, ligatures, punctuation, spelling, source pointers and Roman labels are preserved; common nouns are lowercased. Compiled-index CSS selects reg only, without altering other witnesses.

revisionDesc.change: Authorized human browser-review correction: one provenance note immediately below the index title; reversible sentence-case readings and left-aligned presentation. Original 1856 readings and existing structural identities remain intact.

div.head: Whiston’s chapter headings (compiled index)
div.note: Compiled from the chapter headings printed in the Auburn and Rochester edition of Whiston's translation (Alden & Beardsley, 1856). The arrangement as an index is editorial, not an original printed table of contents.

choice.orig: CONTAINING THE INTERVAL OF FOURTEEN YEARS.
choice.reg: Containing the interval of fourteen years.

choice.orig: FROM ALEXANDER AND ARISTOBULUS'S DEATH TO THE BANISHMENT OF ARCHELAUS.
choice.reg: From Alexander and Aristobulus's death to the banishment of Archelaus.

choice.orig: HOW ANTIPATER WAS HATED BY ALL THE NATION [OF THE JEWS] FOR THE SLAUGHTER OF HIS BRETHREN; AND HOW, FOR THAT REASON, HE GOT INTO PECULIAR FAVOUR WITH HIS FRIENDS AT ROME, BY GIVING THEM MANY PRESENTS; AS HE DID ALSO WITH SATURNINUS, THE PRESIDENT OF SYRIA, AND THE GOVERNORS WHO WERE UNDER HIM; AND CONCERNING HEROD'S WIVES AND CHILDREN.
choice.reg: How Antipater was hated by all the nation [of the Jews] for the slaughter of his brethren; and how, for that reason, he got into peculiar favour with his friends at Rome, by giving them many presents; as he did also with Saturninus, the president of Syria, and the governors who were under him; and concerning Herod's wives and children.

choice.orig: CONCERNING ZAMARIS, THE BABYLONIAN JEW; CONCERNING THE PLOTS LAID BY ANTIPATER AGAINST HIS FATHER; AND SOMEWHAT ABOUT THE PHARISEES.
choice.reg: Concerning Zamaris, the Babylonian Jew; concerning the plots laid by Antipater against his father; and somewhat about the Pharisees.

choice.orig: CONCERNING THE ENMITY BETWEEN HEROD AND PHERORAS; HOW HEROD SENT ANTIPATER TO CÆSAR; AND OF THE DEATH OF PHERORAS.
choice.reg: Concerning the enmity between Herod and Pheroras; how Herod sent Antipater to Cæsar; and of the death of Pheroras.

choice.orig: PHERORAS'S WIFE IS ACCUSED BY HIS FREED-MEN AS GUILTY OF POISONING HIM; AND HOW HEROD, UPON EXAMINING OF THE MATTER BY TORTURE, FOUND THE POISON; BUT SO THAT IT HAD BEEN PREPARED FOR HIMSELF BY HIS SON ANTIPATER; AND, UPON AN INQUIRY BY TORTURE, HE DISCOVERED THE DANGEROUS DESIGNS OF ANTIPATER.
choice.reg: Pheroras's wife is accused by his freed-men as guilty of poisoning him; and how Herod, upon examining of the matter by torture, found the poison; but so that it had been prepared for himself by his son Antipater; and, upon an inquiry by torture, he discovered the dangerous designs of Antipater.

choice.orig: ANTIPATER'S NAVIGATION FROM ROME TO HIS FATHER; AND HOW HE WAS ACCUSED BY NICOLAUS OF DAMASCUS, AND CONDEMNED TO DIE BY HIS FATHER, AND BY QUINTILIUS VARUS, WHO WAS THEN PRESIDENT OF SYRIA; AND HOW HE WAS THEN BOUND TILL CÆSAR SHOULD BE INFORMED OF HIS CAUSE.
choice.reg: Antipater's navigation from Rome to his father; and how he was accused by Nicolaus of Damascus, and condemned to die by his father, and by Quintilius Varus, who was then president of Syria; and how he was then bound till Cæsar should be informed of his cause.

choice.orig: CONCERNING THE DISEASE THAT HEROD FELL INTO, AND THE SEDITION WHICH THE JEWS RAISED THEREUPON; WITH THE PUNISHMENT OF THE SEDITIOUS.
choice.reg: Concerning the disease that Herod fell into, and the sedition which the Jews raised thereupon; with the punishment of the seditious.

choice.orig: HEROD HAS THOUGHTS OF KILLING HIMSELF WITH HIS OWN HAND; AND A LITTLE AFTERWARDS HE ORDERS ANTIPATER TO BE SLAIN.
choice.reg: Herod has thoughts of killing himself with his own hand; and a little afterwards he orders Antipater to be slain.

choice.orig: CONCERNING HEROD'S DEATH, AND TESTAMENT, AND BURIAL.
choice.reg: Concerning Herod's death, and testament, and burial.

choice.orig: HOW THE PEOPLE RAISED A SEDITION AGAINST ARCHELAUS, AND HOW HE SAILED TO ROME.
choice.reg: How the people raised a sedition against Archelaus, and how he sailed to Rome.

choice.orig: A SEDITION OF THE JEWS AGAINST SABINUS; AND HOW VARUS BROUGHT THE AUTHORS OF IT TO PUNISHMENT.
choice.reg: A sedition of the Jews against Sabinus; and how Varus brought the authors of it to punishment.

choice.orig: AN EMBASSAGE OF THE JEWS TO CÆSAR; AND HOW CÆSAR CONFIRMED HEROD'S TESTAMENT.
choice.reg: An embassage of the Jews to Cæsar; and how Cæsar confirmed Herod's testament.

choice.orig: HOW ARCHELAUS, UPON A SECOND ACCUSATION, WAS BANISHED TO VIENNA.
choice.reg: How Archelaus, upon a second accusation, was banished to Vienna.
